review_status: draft v1 - deep reef and wreck snapper

profile.behavior: Aggregates over offshore artificial reefs, deep wrecks, rocky ledges, and hardbottom structures.

factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, inside preferred temperature range for red snapper.
factors.value_notes: A juvenile red snapper habitat-suitability study in the northwestern Gulf found high-value habitat at bottom temperatures of 24–26 °C. NOAA acoustic telemetry off North Carolina found red snapper movement related to bottom-water temperature and vertical thermotaxis. These are juvenile or regional bottom-water relationships, not a universal surface-temperature preference curve; they do not directly validate the configured 16–26 °C range or 19–23 °C ideal.

factors.reason_template: Structure is {value}, highly favored by red snapper.
factors.value_notes: A study of 693 female red snapper off Mississippi examined selection among platforms, artificial reefs, and rigs-to-reefs at multiple depths. BOEM/NOAA sources also document adult association with reefs, rocky bottoms, and underwater objects. This supports structure use but does not validate the exact category preference ordering or numeric map scores across South Florida.

factors.reason_template: Depth is {value} m, in prime red snapper depth zone.
factors.value_notes: BOEM/NOAA sources report red snapper across broad depth ranges, including adults around 7–146 m and juvenile/immature fish at shallower shelf depths. The Mississippi artificial-structure study sampled shallow (<20 m), mid (20–49 m), and deep (50–100 m) habitats. The configured 15–90 m range and 30–60 m ideal overlap these studies but do not establish a single preferred depth across life stages and regions. Depth is an active gate.
